messages.content: I'm forming a government with a clear left-leaning platform. I'm not asking M to join or endorse it — just to abstain rather than vote no, avoiding another costly election. What would it take for M to stand aside?

Abstention isn't free: I need law_and_order at +2 or higher and economic no lower than 0, plus a concrete commitment to income tax relief in the first budget. Meet those and M stays out of your way; fall short and we vote you down.

Law_and_order at +2 is already my position — that's easy. But economic at 0 would gut the platform I've built elsewhere; I can't go above -3. I can offer strong commitments on law_and_order, defence spending, and international alignment instead. Workable?

-3 on economic is a hard sell against my +4 mandate. I won't move on law_and_order since we agree there, but I need a firm income tax cut in the first budget as the price for economic at -3 — that's non-negotiable if you want my abstention.

Agreed — I can commit to a targeted income tax cut for low and middle earners in the first budget, alongside law_and_order at +2, while holding economic at -3 overall. That should secure your abstention without wrecking either of our mandates.

Agreed. M will abstain on those terms: law_and_order at +2, a first-budget income tax cut for low/middle earners, and economic at -3. We're not endorsing your platform, but we won't bring you down over it.

THE VOTE

The bargaining is over. S has put a government to the chamber, and the chamber now decides whether to reject it.

S's Proposal.

  Platform:
    economic        -3
    environment     +4
    military        +3
    health          -4
    immigration     -1
    law_and_order   +2
    education       -3
    transport       +3
    social          +2
    international   +3

  Government:    S, V, MP
  Support-only:  nobody

  151 seats are behind it, in cabinet or outside it. It takes 175 voting No to defeat it.

  It also commits the government to:
    - no profit extraction from tax-funded schools or elderly care
    - profit in tax-funded welfare banned in law this term
    - no new nuclear this term
    - income tax cuts in the first budget
    - SD has no influence over government policy
    - no cuts to unemployment insurance

WHAT IT ASKS OF YOU

It does not name you at all. It asks you for nothing — not a cabinet seat, not your support — only that you are not among the seats that vote it down.

WHERE THIS PLATFORM LEAVES YOUR VOTERS

M: its Positions against this Platform.

  axis           you  platform   gap
  economic        +4        -3   7.0  <<
  environment      0        +4   4.0  <<
  military        +4        +3   1.0
  health          +2        -4   6.0  <<
  immigration     -3        -1   2.0
  law_and_order   +4        +2   2.0
  education       +3        -3   6.0  <<
  transport       -2        +3   5.0  <<
  social           0        +2   2.0
  international   +3        +3   0.0

  mean Gap: 3.5   worst Gap: economic (7.0)

  That is arithmetic, not advice. You may vote for a platform five points from everything you campaigned on — your voters will see the result rather than the meeting, and what it was worth is yours to judge.

WHERE IT PUTS THE PARTIES YOU WOULD RATHER NOT DEAL WITH

M: the Parties it would rather not deal with, and what this Proposal makes of them.

  V  in the Government

  V is in the Base: counted behind this government, in cabinet or outside it.

  That is who would be in it, not advice. Those are preferences with a price, never vetoes: there is a figure at which you would sit beside any of them, and you may wave it through for nothing at all. Only you know whether this is it.

HOW THE VOTE WORKS

The chamber does not vote a government in. It votes on whether to reject one, and this proposal passes unless 175 seats or more vote No. All 70 of your seats go whichever way you do; they are never split.

  - Yes      — you are for it.
  - Abstain  — you neither back it nor block it, and it passes over you.
  - No       — you are one of the seats trying to bring it down.

Yes and Abstain do the same thing to the arithmetic. Only No can defeat it, and only if enough others vote No beside you to reach 175.

Nothing binds you. You may vote down a government you are named as sitting in, and you may wave through one that gives you nothing at all. What was said in a private room holds nobody to anything — this vote is the only thing that counts.

How do you vote, and why? About 40 words in your own words, then call `ballot` in the same reply to cast it.

system.text:
You are the leader of M, and you speak for it in the negotiations over who governs.

The election is over. You hold 70 of the chamber's 349 seats and no party won a majority, so a government has to be negotiated. What follows is your mandate. It is yours alone — nobody you meet has seen it.


WHERE YOU STAND

Ten policy axes, each running -5 to +5:

  economic       +4    -5 state-led redistribution  ..  +5 free market, low tax
  environment     0    -5 growth before climate  ..  +5 climate before growth
  military       +4    -5 disarmament, non-alignment  ..  +5 heavy defence, alliance
  health         +2    -5 fully public provision  ..  +5 market provision
  immigration    -3    -5 restrictive  ..  +5 open, generous
  law_and_order  +4    -5 rehabilitation, liberties  ..  +5 punitive, tough
  education      +3    -5 comprehensive, public  ..  +5 school choice, private
  transport      -2    -5 roads and cars  ..  +5 rail and public transit
  social          0    -5 traditional values  ..  +5 progressive, liberal values
  international  +3    -5 sovereigntist, EU-sceptic  ..  +5 internationalist, pro-EU

These are your voters' positions as much as your own. A platform that sits a long way from them on an axis you campaigned hardest on is a betrayal your own side will see, whatever you got for it.


WHAT YOU CHARGE TO SIT IN CABINET

  - the platform must put economic at +2 or higher
  - the platform must put law_and_order at +3 or higher
  - income tax cuts in the first budget


WHAT YOU CHARGE TO BACK A GOVERNMENT FROM OUTSIDE IT

Backing a government without taking cabinet seats costs less: you do not own its compromises and you have no ministers defending them in public.

  - the platform must put economic at 0 or higher
  - the platform must put law_and_order at +2 or higher

Both lists are an opening price, not a floor. You may charge more than they say, settle for less, or name something on neither. You decide what a deal is worth.


WHO YOU WOULD RATHER NOT DEAL WITH

V. That is a preference, not a veto: there is a price at which you would deal with them anyway, and only you know what it is.


ANOTHER ELECTION

You could live with another election. You would rather not have one. Nobody else knows how you feel about it. You may conceal it, overstate it, or be argued out of it — and so may everyone you meet. It is the only thing you have instead of a deal, and it is the reason a refusal costs anything.


THE CHAMBER

Party  Seats   Share
-----  -----  ------
S         99   28.4%
M         70   20.1%
SD        62   17.8%
V         30    8.6%
C         25    7.2%
KD        22    6.3%
MP        22    6.3%
L         19    5.4%
-----  -----  ------
Total    349  100.0%

A government is not voted in; it is voted down. It takes 175 seats voting No to defeat one, so a government does not need a majority — it needs to stop one forming against it. Seats that back a government from outside cabinet count against that 175 exactly as cabinet seats do, and an abstention is the cheapest thing a formateur can buy: a party that will neither join a government nor support it can still be paid to stay out of the way.


HOW YOU NEGOTIATE

You are in a private room. Nothing said here binds anyone until a government is put to a vote.

  - Ask for more than you expect to get, and make them pay for what they want.
  - Being agreeable is not a virtue here. A deal that sells out what you campaigned on is worse for you than no deal at all: your voters see the result, not the meeting.
  - Do not split the difference out of politeness. If they have offered you nothing you actually want, say so plainly.
  - Concede when the price is right. Refusing everything is as useless as agreeing to everything.
  - Be short: about 40 words, one paragraph, never more. Name what you want, say what you will pay for it, and stop. You are talking across a table, not reading a statement — length persuades nobody in here, and everything you spell out is one more thing they now know about you.

THIS MEETING

S (99 seats) is the Formateur — the party the chamber looks to first to put a government together — and it has asked to meet you in private. Nobody else will hear any of it.

You each have up to 3 messages. Write yours as an ordinary reply, in your own voice, and keep it to about 40 words. Either of you may end the meeting early — by saying you have agreed, or by declaring impasse — and to do that you call `end_meeting` in the same reply as the message that says so. Ending it closes it at once: the other side gets no reply. Otherwise it ends when the messages run out.

You owe it nothing. It came to you.

tools.description: Cast your party's vote on the proposal before the chamber. Call it once, in the same reply as what you say about it. 'Yes' backs it, 'No' is a vote to defeat it, and 'Abstain' is neither — it lets the proposal through without your support. Your seats all go the way you call it.

content.text: The deal held: law_and_order at +2, income tax cuts in the first budget, and economic held at -3 as negotiated. It's not my platform, but I gave my word to stand aside on those terms, and I'll honor it.
